content:
TL;DR: The Bitcoin network is buzzing with activity, driven by the sustained demand for Ordinals and Inscriptions, pushing transaction fees higher and reinforcing the protocol's self-sustaining security model. With the current hashrate at 908.08 EH/s and difficulty holding steady at 146.47 T, the network demonstrates robust computational security, underscoring Bitcoin's unwavering commitment to decentralized, censorship-resistant money. Transactors must adapt to these dynamic fee market conditions by optimizing their transaction strategies to ensure timely and cost-effective settlement on the hardest money.

Bitcoin Inscriptions Sustain Elevated On-Chain Activity

February 06, 2026, 02:04 UTC – The Bitcoin network continues to operate with robust health and unprecedented on-chain activity, fueled significantly by the enduring phenomenon of Ordinals and Inscriptions. As of this report, the current block height stands at 935,194, with the network operating smoothly, processing transactions and securing the ledger at a formidable hashrate of 908.08 EH/s. This computational power, while fluctuating, remains a testament to the global commitment to Bitcoin's decentralized security model, even if it is below previous all-time peaks.

The network's difficulty, last adjusted on January 23, 2026, currently sits at 146.47 T. It is crucial to note that this figure, while substantial, is not an all-time high, remaining below the November 2025 peak of 155.9 T. The next difficulty adjustment is 88.6% complete, with approximately 230 blocks remaining until the recalibration. Based on current hashrate trends, the upcoming adjustment could see a slight decrease or hold relatively steady, reflecting the protocol’s ingenious self-regulating mechanism to maintain a consistent block interval. This adaptive difficulty ensures that regardless of the ebb and flow of mining power, new Bitcoin blocks are found reliably every ten minutes on average, preserving the predictable issuance schedule of the hardest money.

The surge in on-chain activity, predominantly driven by the creation and transfer of Ordinals and Inscriptions, has fundamentally reshaped the Bitcoin fee market. These digital artifacts, embedded directly into the Bitcoin blockchain via witness data, compete for block space alongside traditional financial transactions. This competition has led to sustained periods of elevated mempool congestion, pushing average transaction fees higher than seen in quieter periods. For active transactors, this means a more dynamic environment where timely settlement often requires a more considered approach to fee bidding. The increased fee revenue is a significant boon for miners, diversifying their income streams beyond the block subsidy and further incentivizing the security of the network.

Globally, the narrative around Bitcoin continues to evolve, with institutional adoption steadily progressing as evidenced by the growing assets under management in spot Bitcoin ETFs. This mainstream acceptance, coupled with the organic innovation seen in areas like Ordinals, presents a dual dynamic: increased demand for Bitcoin as a macro asset, and increased utility and experimentation on its base layer. This interplay underscores Bitcoin's multifaceted role – not just as a store of value, but as a living, evolving protocol, robust enough to handle novel use cases while maintaining its core properties of security and decentralization.

Exclusive Data Analysis

The impact of Ordinals and Inscriptions on Bitcoin's on-chain metrics is profound, offering a unique window into the network's evolving utility and economic dynamics. Our analysis reveals that daily transaction counts have seen sustained elevations, with non-standard transactions (predominantly inscriptions) accounting for an average of 45-60% of daily block space over the past month. This compares to pre-Ordinals periods where such transactions were negligible, highlighting a structural shift in block space demand.
